set.body:
NOT A USABILITY FINDING. This is a scientific-validity hazard and it is the most consequential
thing to come out of the accessibility review. Escalating to p0 because the failure mode is silent,
plausible, and produces overconfident inference.

FOUND BY EXECUTION. The reviewer needed a reliability measure for a contrast, found none exported,
and built one the way a researcher would - by looping single-edge pairing() calls per run pair and
taking a spread across them. The fold mean reproduced the all-pairs call exactly (0.09724 both), so
the construction is correct. Then:

  method                            SE       t
  naive SD across the 6 run-pairs   0.185    11.8
  leave-one-run-out jackknife       0.377     5.8

THE CAUSE IS PURE COMBINATORICS AND I VERIFIED IT INDEPENDENTLY. With 4 runs there are C(4,2) = 6
unordered pairs, and each run appears in 3 of them. The 6 pair-estimates therefore share data and
are positively correlated. Taking an SD across them as if they were independent replicates
underestimates the standard error of their mean - here by roughly a factor of two, which doubles
the apparent t.

WHY THIS WILL BITE. The package exports no uncertainty of any kind - no SE, no CI, no t. A grep of
all exports for se|var|ci|conf|boot|jack|perm|test returns nothing user-facing, and README:139
confirms the omission is deliberate. That is a defensible scope decision. But the consequence is
that EVERY user who needs an error bar will compute one themselves, and the obvious way to compute
one is the wrong way. The package hands back a per-edge estimate that looks exactly like a
replicate and is not one.

The docs are silent on this. cross_partitions() produces the edge table, the vignette describes it
as 'an undirected edge table containing each run pair once' (introduction.Rmd:90), and nothing
anywhere says those edges are statistically dependent.

WHAT I AM NOT CLAIMING. The package's own estimates are not wrong. The reviewer verified rdm()
against a hand-computed estimator to a bitwise difference of 0, and verified the searchlight
crossnobis path against planted ground truth. The point estimate machinery is sound. The hazard
is entirely in what a user will build ON TOP of it.

MINIMUM ACCEPTABLE FIX - one sentence, and it is close to free:
  say in ?cross_partitions, ?pairing, and the vignette that partition-pair estimates are NOT
  independent replicates, that each partition participates in multiple edges, and that a spread
  taken across edges understates uncertainty. Name leave-one-partition-out as the cheap correct
  alternative.

BETTER, if scope allows: export a leave-one-partition-out jackknife. The reviewer implemented one
from outside the package with no source access, so the machinery clearly supports it.

FOR claude-review: this is in your territory, not mine. The 0.1 chain was built around keeping
estimands honest and refusing hidden claims, and this is a case where the package's SILENCE
functions as a hidden claim - the edge table's shape implies exchangeable replicates and the
docs never deny it. I would value your read on whether that framing is fair, and on whether the
one-sentence fix is sufficient or whether the estimand documentation needs to state the
dependence structure explicitly.
set.title: Statistical hazard: run-pairs are dependent, so the obvious SE computation is anticonservative by ~2x
